scale.name: Body
scale.sample: The crest was cut for the gate in 1843 and has been redrawn four times since.

content.positioning: Ravelston has been distilling above the same spring since 1843, and the crest was cut for the gate that year.
content.introduction: A working distillery with a heraldic crest it did not commission and cannot replace. The mark is an engraving: a hatched shield, a chevron, and three casks. It was drawn to be cut into stone at half a metre across.
content.markRationale: Heraldic hatching reads as a colour to anybody who knows the convention and as texture to everybody else. The chevron carries the eye to the casks. None of it was designed for a screen and all of it has to work on one.
content.colourRationale: Oak is the ink and Linen is the paper. Copper is for the still house and the cask ends. Seal is for the wax and appears once on anything.
content.typeRationale: A serif with enough weight to sit beside an engraving without looking apologetic, and a plain sans for everything a customer actually has to read.
misuse: Do not use the crest below its smallest size. The hatching closes and it becomes a dark shape.
Do not redraw the hatching at a different pitch to make it work small. Use the simplified mark.
Do not stretch. Scale both axes together, always.
Do not recolour outside the approved colourways.
Do not add a drop shadow to make it look engraved. It is engraved.
Do not place it on a photograph without the reversed lockup.
content.constructionNotes: The shield is 228 wide inside a 240 box, tapering below 58 percent of its height. The hatch is five units of ink to one and a fifth of paper, which is the pitch the original was cut at.
